fruits.extendedStory: Work on the present church started in 1075, on ground that had drawn people since 801. Romanesque is the underlying manner, though Fernando de Casas Novoa dressed the west front much later. It rises around 75 metres. Arrive on foot after weeks of walking and this facade is the finish line. Pilgrims still sit down in front of it to take that in.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Am heutigen Bau begann man 1075, auf Boden, der schon seit 801 Menschen anzog. Zugrunde liegt die romanische Weise, doch Fernando de Casas Novoa kleidete die Westfront viel später neu ein. Sie ragt etwa 75 Meter auf. Wer nach Wochen zu Fuß ankommt, sieht in dieser Fassade das Ziel. Pilger setzen sich noch immer davor hin, um das zu begreifen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Work on the present church started in 1075, on ground that had drawn people since 801. Romanesque is the underlying manner, though Fernando de Casas Novoa dressed the west front much later. It rises around 75 metres. Arrive on foot after weeks of walking and this facade is the finish line. Pilgrims still sit down in front of it to take that in.

localizedStory.de: Jeder Weg, der Camino heißt, endet an dieser Kirche. Der Bau begann 1075.
localizedStory.en: Every road called the Camino ends at this church. Building began in 1075.

fruits.name: Catedral de Santiago de Compostela
fruits.story: Every road called the Camino ends at this church. Building began in 1075.

fruits.extendedStory: Obradoiro means the workshop, and it refers to the stonemasons' yard that operated behind the cathedral while building went on. Each of the four sides now carries a different institution: cathedral to the east, town hall opposite, pilgrims' hostel north, university south. Kilometre zero sits in the middle. Every road that calls itself a way to Santiago finishes here, on these paving stones.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Obradoiro heißt Werkstatt und meint den Steinmetzhof, der hinter dem Dom arbeitete, solange gebaut wurde. Jede der vier Seiten trägt heute eine andere Einrichtung: Dom im Osten, Rathaus gegenüber, Pilgerherberge im Norden, Universität im Süden. In der Mitte liegt Kilometer null. Jeder Weg, der sich Weg nach Santiago nennt, endet hier, auf diesen Steinen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Obradoiro means the workshop, and it refers to the stonemasons' yard that operated behind the cathedral while building went on. Each of the four sides now carries a different institution: cathedral to the east, town hall opposite, pilgrims' hostel north, university south. Kilometre zero sits in the middle. Every road that calls itself a way to Santiago finishes here, on these paving stones.

localizedStory.de: Vier Seiten, vier Einrichtungen. Dom im Osten, Rathaus im Westen, Pilgerherberge im Norden, Universität im Süden.
localizedStory.en: Four sides, four institutions. Cathedral east, town hall west, pilgrims' hostel north, university south.

fruits.name: Praza do Obradoiro
fruits.story: Four sides, four institutions. Cathedral east, town hall west, pilgrims' hostel north, university south.

fruits.extendedStory: Until about 1611 this ground held graves. The cathedral chapter then turned it over to public use. The master Francisco Fernandez de Araujo did the work, under the canon Jose Vega y Verdugo. They closed the cathedral's eastern side behind one long wall. Set into that wall is the Holy Door, opened in a Holy Year.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Bis etwa 1611 lagen hier Gräber. Dann gab das Domkapitel den Boden für die Öffentlichkeit frei. Meister Francisco Fernandez de Araujo führte die Arbeit aus, unter dem Kanoniker Jose Vega y Verdugo. Man schloss dabei die Ostseite des Doms hinter einer langen Mauer. In dieser Mauer sitzt die Heilige Pforte, die sich im Heiligen Jahr öffnet.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Until about 1611 this ground held graves. The cathedral chapter then turned it over to public use. The master Francisco Fernandez de Araujo did the work, under the canon Jose Vega y Verdugo. They closed the cathedral's eastern side behind one long wall. Set into that wall is the Holy Door, opened in a Holy Year.

localizedStory.de: Die untere Hälfte dieses Platzes heißt noch Quintana der Toten. Hier lag ein Friedhof.
localizedStory.en: The lower half of this square is still called the Quintana of the Dead. It was a burial ground.

fruits.name: Praza da Quintana de Mortos
fruits.story: The lower half of this square is still called the Quintana of the Dead. It was a burial ground.

fruits.extendedStory: Enrique Egas built this from 1511, in the Plateresque manner. Plateresque means stonework cut as finely as a silversmith works metal, and the doorway is where it all goes. It was raised to shelter pilgrims who had walked a very long way. It stands on the north side of the Obradoiro, facing the cathedral across the square. People still sleep here at the end of the road.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Enrique Egas baute dies ab 1511, im plateresken Stil. Plateresk heißt Steinwerk, so fein geschnitten, wie ein Silberschmied Metall bearbeitet, und alles davon sitzt am Portal. Errichtet wurde es, um Pilger aufzunehmen, die einen sehr weiten Weg hinter sich hatten. Es steht an der Nordseite des Obradoiro, dem Dom gegenüber. Menschen schlafen hier noch immer am Ende des Wegs.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Enrique Egas built this from 1511, in the Plateresque manner. Plateresque means stonework cut as finely as a silversmith works metal, and the doorway is where it all goes. It was raised to shelter pilgrims who had walked a very long way. It stands on the north side of the Obradoiro, facing the cathedral across the square. People still sleep here at the end of the road.

localizedStory.de: 1511 erbaut, um Pilger aufzunehmen, die hierher gelaufen waren. Es nimmt noch immer Gäste auf.
localizedStory.en: Built in 1511 to shelter pilgrims who had walked here. It still takes guests.

fruits.name: Parador Hostal dos Reis Católicos
fruits.story: Built in 1511 to shelter pilgrims who had walked here. It still takes guests.

fruits.extendedStory: Joaquin Vaquero Palacios designed this market and it took from 1938 to 1945 to build, in eight stone naves. It replaced the old city market, pulled down in 1937, on a spot where trading had gone on since the eighteenth century. Locals shop here rather than perform for anyone. That is exactly why it draws more visitors than anywhere in Santiago except the cathedral.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Joaquin Vaquero Palacios entwarf diesen Markt, gebaut von 1938 bis 1945, in acht steinernen Hallen. Er ersetzte den alten Stadtmarkt, 1937 abgerissen, an einer Stelle, an der seit dem achtzehnten Jahrhundert gehandelt wurde. Die Leute kaufen hier ein und führen nichts vor. Genau darum kommen hierher mehr Besucher als irgendwo sonst in Santiago, den Dom ausgenommen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Joaquin Vaquero Palacios designed this market and it took from 1938 to 1945 to build, in eight stone naves. It replaced the old city market, pulled down in 1937, on a spot where trading had gone on since the eighteenth century. Locals shop here rather than perform for anyone. That is exactly why it draws more visitors than anywhere in Santiago except the cathedral.

localizedStory.de: Acht steinerne Hallen voller Fisch, Käse und Brot. Nach dem Dom geht die Stadt hierher.
localizedStory.en: Eight stone naves full of fish, cheese and bread. After the cathedral, this is where the city goes.

fruits.name: Mercado de Abastos de Santiago
fruits.story: Eight stone naves full of fish, cheese and bread. After the cathedral, this is where the city goes.

fruits.extendedStory: Juan de Álava built this from 1522, in the Spanish Renaissance manner. That style likes a flat wall broken by one very worked doorway, so the carving is concentrated where you go in. This was where the university began. Step through into the courtyard: the noise of the street stops at the arch, which is roughly the point of a cloister.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Juan de Álava baute dies ab 1522, in spanischer Renaissance. Dieser Stil mag eine glatte Wand mit einem reich gearbeiteten Portal, das Schnitzwerk sitzt also dort, wo man hineingeht. Hier begann die Universität. Tritt in den Innenhof: der Lärm der Straße endet am Bogen, und ungefähr dafür ist ein Kreuzgang da.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Juan de Álava built this from 1522, in the Spanish Renaissance manner. That style likes a flat wall broken by one very worked doorway, so the carving is concentrated where you go in. This was where the university began. Step through into the courtyard: the noise of the street stops at the arch, which is roughly the point of a cloister.

localizedStory.de: Die Universität begann hier 1522, in einem Hofgebäude von Juan de Álava.
localizedStory.en: The university started here in 1522, in a courtyard building by Juan de Álava.

fruits.name: Colexio de Fonseca
fruits.story: The university started here in 1522, in a courtyard building by Juan de Álava.

fruits.extendedStory: Monks have been on this hill since 899, and a house stood here by the year 1000 and again in 1102. What you walk past now is mostly the rebuilding that started in 1590, in the baroque manner. Baroque wants weight and drama, and it got both here. The scale is startling for a house of monks. The cathedral is a few streets away, and this was never meant to come second to it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Seit 899 sind Mönche auf diesem Hügel, um das Jahr 1000 stand hier ein Haus und 1102 erneut. Woran man heute vorbeigeht, ist überwiegend der Neubau ab 1590, barock. Barock will Gewicht und Wirkung, und beides bekam er hier. Für ein Mönchshaus ist der Maßstab verblüffend. Unter der Front lohnt der Gedanke, dass der Dom wenige Gassen entfernt liegt und dies ihm nie nachstehen sollte.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Monks have been on this hill since 899, and a house stood here by the year 1000 and again in 1102. What you walk past now is mostly the rebuilding that started in 1590, in the baroque manner. Baroque wants weight and drama, and it got both here. The scale is startling for a house of monks. The cathedral is a few streets away, and this was never meant to come second to it.

localizedStory.de: Ein Kloster, dessen Geschichte auf diesem Hügel bis 899 zurückreicht, ab 1590 barock neu gebaut.
localizedStory.en: A monastery whose story on this hill reaches back to 899, rebuilt in baroque style from 1590.

fruits.name: Mosteiro e Igrexa de San Martiño Piñario e Seminario Maior
fruits.story: A monastery whose story on this hill reaches back to 899, rebuilt in baroque style from 1590.

fruits.extendedStory: This was the main gate, where those walking the French Way finally entered the city. It had a double arch with a square tower on either side. Each new archbishop was met right here by the chief chaplain, who held out the keys of Compostela on a tray. The gate was taken down between 1800 and 1835. The name stayed on the street, and pilgrims still come in this way without a gate to walk through.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Dies war das Haupttor, durch das die Pilger des Französischen Wegs endlich in die Stadt kamen. Es hatte einen Doppelbogen und je einen viereckigen Turm an den Seiten. Jeden neuen Erzbischof empfing hier der Oberkaplan und hielt ihm die Schlüssel Compostelas auf einem Tablett hin. Zwischen 1800 und 1835 wurde das Tor abgetragen. Der Name blieb an der Straße, und Pilger kommen weiter hier herein, nur ohne Tor.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This was the main gate, where those walking the French Way finally entered the city. It had a double arch with a square tower on either side. Each new archbishop was met right here by the chief chaplain, who held out the keys of Compostela on a tray. The gate was taken down between 1800 and 1835. The name stayed on the street, and pilgrims still come in this way without a gate to walk through.

localizedStory.de: Pilger auf dem Französischen Weg betraten die Stadt durch dieses Tor. Nichts davon ist geblieben.
localizedStory.en: Pilgrims on the French Way came into the city through this gate. Nothing of it is left.

fruits.name: Porta do Camiño
fruits.story: Pilgrims on the French Way came into the city through this gate. Nothing of it is left.

fruits.extendedStory: The building is the Casa Grande do Pozo on Rua do Vilar. The cathedral chapter owned it from the fifteenth century into the nineteenth. Its name comes from the well inside it, which could supply every public fountain in the city. That made the house worth holding onto. Manuel Pereiro Caeiro rebuilt much of it late in the nineteenth century. The well is still down on the ground floor.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Haus ist die Casa Grande do Pozo an der Rua do Vilar. Das Domkapitel besaß es vom fünfzehnten bis ins neunzehnte Jahrhundert. Sein Name kommt vom Brunnen darin, der jeden öffentlichen Brunnen der Stadt versorgen konnte. Das machte das Haus wertvoll. Manuel Pereiro Caeiro baute es Ende des neunzehnten Jahrhunderts weitgehend um, und der Brunnen liegt noch unten im Erdgeschoss.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The building is the Casa Grande do Pozo on Rua do Vilar. The cathedral chapter owned it from the fifteenth century into the nineteenth. Its name comes from the well inside it, which could supply every public fountain in the city. That made the house worth holding onto. Manuel Pereiro Caeiro rebuilt much of it late in the nineteenth century. The well is still down on the ground floor.

localizedStory.de: Im Erdgeschoss liegt der Brunnen, nach dem dieses Haus heißt. Er speiste einst die Stadtbrunnen.
localizedStory.en: Down on the ground floor is the well this house is named for. It once fed the city's fountains.

fruits.name: Biblioteca Afundación Santiago de Compostela
fruits.story: Down on the ground floor is the well this house is named for. It once fed the city's fountains.

fruits.extendedStory: Jesuits held this site until 1767, when Carlos III expelled the order and the crown passed their Santiago property to the university. Miguel Ferro Caaveiro drew the earliest scheme. Melchor de Prado e Marino reworked it, and the credit generally goes to him. Building ran from 1769 to 1805. A square named for a university sits where a religious order was turned out.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Bis 1767 gehörte dieses Gelände den Jesuiten, dann vertrieb Carlos III. den Orden und die Krone gab ihren Besitz in Santiago der Universität. Miguel Ferro Caaveiro entwarf den Plan. Melchor de Prado e Marino arbeitete ihn um, und ihm schreibt man das Werk meist zu. Gebaut wurde von 1769 bis 1805. Ein Platz mit dem Namen der Universität liegt dort, wo ein Orden weichen musste.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Jesuits held this site until 1767, when Carlos III expelled the order and the crown passed their Santiago property to the university. Miguel Ferro Caaveiro drew the earliest scheme. Melchor de Prado e Marino reworked it, and the credit generally goes to him. Building ran from 1769 to 1805. A square named for a university sits where a religious order was turned out.

localizedStory.de: Hier stand ein Jesuitenkolleg, bis ein König den Orden vertrieb und den Grund der Universität übergab.
localizedStory.en: A Jesuit college stood here until a king expelled the order and handed the ground to the university.

fruits.name: Praza da Universidade
fruits.story: A Jesuit college stood here until a king expelled the order and handed the ground to the university.
